neighbours.label: Best guess, weak: the clause after a degree-threshold phrase ('to the point that …', 'to the extent that …', 'beyond a certain point')
fire: The river had been shrinking for years, slowly drying to the point that it now barely reaches the sea.
Her voice had grown hoarse to the extent that she could hardly be heard in the back row.
The old bridge had rusted to the point that it was no longer safe for trucks.
Economists argue that, beyond a certain point, higher taxes reduce the total revenue collected.
The paint had faded to the extent that the original colours could not be guessed.
The company cut its staff to the point that it has now closed two of its offices.
Doctors warn that, past a certain point, more exercise brings no further benefit.
The town had emptied to the point that the school has now shut its doors.
quiet: The river had been shrinking for years, and farmers along its banks were worried.
Her voice was hoarse, but she sang in the back row anyway.
The old bridge was rusty, yet trucks crossed it every day.
Economists argue that higher taxes fund schools, roads and hospitals.
The paint was faded, and nobody remembered the original colours.
The company hired new staff and opened two more offices.
Doctors recommend regular exercise for people of every age.
The town was small, and the school stood next to the church.

notes: Card top examples are mixed (to the point that, beyond a certain point, SHUTDOWN, 关闭, .wait()). Probes of the threshold reading reached only 0.06-0.13 of max, so I expect this to fail; registered to record that honestly.
